Why go: a newer, better-kept scooter than the roadside average

Scooters are the cheapest way to get around Koh Samui, and you can rent one from almost every street corner. The difference is in the bike and the paperwork: these are recent-model Yamaha and Honda scooters with two helmets, handed over with an inspection and briefing, and booked in advance at a fixed price. Weekly and monthly rates make them good value for longer stays.

What you'll do

Collect the scooter at 09:00 at the office in Maret, near Lamai, or ask us about delivery. You check and photograph the bike with the staff, sign the agreement, leave a deposit and ride away. Return it at 09:00 on your last day with the same fuel level.

Who it suits

  • Experienced riders with the right licence who want freedom to explore beaches and viewpoints.
  • Long-stay visitors and remote workers looking for a monthly rate.

Who should choose something else

  • First-time riders: Samui's roads are not the place to learn. Use a private van with driver or taxis.
  • Families with children: a car is safer. See car rental on Koh Samui.

Good to know

  • Licence: police run regular checkpoints; riding without a motorcycle licence or helmet means a fine and, more importantly, no insurance cover.
  • Scams: photograph every scratch at handover and never leave your passport if a cash deposit is possible. See common scams.
  • Roads: the ring road is busy, the hill roads are steep and sand on corners causes many falls. See Koh Samui roads.

Before you book

Check your licence first: an International Driving Permit only covers motorcycles if the motorcycle category is stamped. Choose the Aerox for solo riding on the ring road, or the ADV 160 if two of you will ride often or you plan to explore the hills.
